title: India’s Javelin Deal: The Unending Loop of Procurement
author: Dinakar Peri
text:
Credit: Lockheed Martin
“BIG news! India plans to buy the battle-tested Javelin anti-tank system,” U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor announced on X on August 28, as the Indian Army signed the letter of offer and acceptance (LOA) for the purchase of the missile system through the foreign military sales (FMS) route, also adding that it’s opening the door to “co-production possibilities.” For the Indian Army, it marks 16 years of ups and downs and the long lead time to fill a critical capability gap in anti-tank guided missiles (ATGM), even if only piecemeal.The Javelin is a versatile, one-man-portable and platform-mounted fire-and-forget anti-tank precision weapon system that is capable of defeating all kinds of armor and fortified positions. It is in service with more than 25 countries, including the U.S. Army and the U.S. Marine Corps.[...]
